correctness.rationale: For each odd prime p and characteristic-p field, the binomial identity and path count locate precisely six possible output coordinates. Necessity follows from consecutive products and a unique two-jump path. Explicit sparse-root constructions split into every possible leading-coordinate and boundary-zero case; each case has been checked against matrix powering in prime fields p=3 and 5. The disjoint target-stratum count is symbolic. Verification includes complete p=3 source enumeration over 3^12 effective inputs, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact six-coordinate iff and all-odd-prime counting polynomial against the closest power-map and verbal-width primary papers and accessible own claims. Bier gives group generation and width two, Dolfi et al. give lower bounds and the already-known isolated value 585, and earlier own work handles only p=2. None of these implies the odd-prime elementwise criterion; an unidentified more general source remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The size p+3 is forced by the established first width-two threshold for p-power words. The theorem solves the exact image-membership problem in this natural boundary family simultaneously for all odd primes and all extension fields; it distinguishes product-of-two-powers from an individual power by explicit coordinate obstructions and gives the uniform image-density polynomial. This is more informative than the known properness and numerical examples.
